**Why.** A token transfer is a special case of a meta-transaction (owner); keeping it as a typed struct (`to`, `value`, `entryRef`) lets outside wallets show "send value to to" instead of opaque `data` (owner G1 (b)), and `mtxExecuteTransfer` takes the struct as given so a payment can use a client-chosen lane (owner G6).
**Cost if wrong.** Without the typed struct a transfer would be hex in every outside wallet; without the struct entry a payment could use only `payLane`.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G1, G6, §3 GC-1, GC-4, GC-5.

### CTR-MTX-24 — mtxBatchTransfer beside mtxBatch
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-24 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** With transfers in their own struct, `mtxBatch(MetaTransaction[])` can no longer carry the payments the node batches; a typed batch keeps that saving (owner G5 1a) under the same atomic rules, and a batch never mixes the two structs.
**Cost if wrong.** Payments could no longer be batched, or one batch function would have to decode two structs.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G5, §3 GC-5.

### CTR-MTX-25 — One SigCheck
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-25 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One internal `SigCheck` (ECDSA low-s, ERC-1271 with the gas-cap rule, the HIP-632 hook) serves `MetaTxBase`, `SCaaSDex`, `MandateWallet` and `SmartKeyAccount`; `SigLib`, which has no importer, is deleted. Today the check is written six times and the HIP-632 override four times.
**Cost if wrong.** Copies drift: a fix to the gas cap or the low-s rule lands in one contract and not in the others.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §1, §4.

Change (2026-10-30, **owner ruling D1** — owner 2026-10-30, after the 2026-10-29 EIP-7702 hot-wallet drain: "an EOA must really sign — no delegation at all; an EOA must not run code"; status: current, decided (owner); commits: `no7702` `5ddc577d`, sizes `684f5643`, node `dad611dc`): on the address path a 7702 designator account signs by its own key only, never ERC-1271 through the delegate. `SigCheck.isValid`: `!isContract(signer)` (no code, or code that is exactly `0xef0100 ‖ delegate`, 23 bytes) ⇒ ECDSA low-s only; other code ⇒ ERC-1271 only, caps and the EIP-150 floor unchanged. New helpers `isDesignator` (`extcodesize == 23`, then a 3-byte `extcodecopy` compared with `0xef0100`), `isContract` (as before), `requireNotDelegated` and `error CallerDelegated(address caller)` (defined once, in the library; it reaches the ABI of every token, `MandateWallet`, `SmartKeyAccount`, `SCaaSDex` and `OpenFactory`). Callers: `MetaTxBase` / `MtxPipelineLib` (`mtxExecute*`, the transfers, pay-meta, the UA ledger's native `from`), `SCaaSDex` orders / cancels / `mtxInvalidateNonces`, `mtxWrap` / `uaWrap`, `MandateWallet`, `SmartKeyAccount`; the node's DEX venue `valid_sig` mirrors it (`chain::is_contract`), and the node's gas guard gives a designator payer no ERC-1271 gas floor (`Chain::is_contract_at` replaces `has_code`). Supersedes the 2026-10-28 rule (CTR-MTX-27 change of that date). Why: a delegate's ERC-1271 lets whatever code the account is delegated to — a sweeper after one phishing signature — sign every relayable action as the account (audit A1); the base key is root at protocol level, so key-only adds no restriction a sweeper could not already bypass with the key. Cost if wrong: a 7702 wallet's session keys or passkeys cannot sign for SCaaS; its base key still can. Tests flipped: `SigCheck.t.sol` `test_isValid_7702_ctrUa24` (the delegate is never called: `expectCall` count 0), `UALedger` `test_7702_nativeFrom`, `UAReceiverFee` `test_uaPayReceiverFee_7702Payee`, parity rows `ok_e7702_viaDelegate*` → `err_e7702_viaDelegate*` (12 rows, `PARITY_WRITE=1`), node `a_7702_maker_signs_with_its_key_only`. Gas (parity fixture): designator base-key rows −260, a designator's bad signature −5,640 (the delegate is no longer called), ERC-1271 wallet signers +31 / −246. Source: the EIP-7702 audit of 2026-10-30 (`research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md`) §3, §6.

### CTR-MTX-26 — Payment metadata by commitment: mtxPayMeta / uaPayMeta
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-26 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-26 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner asked for metadata on a payment id. `payId = keccak256("scaas.pay.meta" ‖ salt ‖ keccak256(meta))`
lets the existing signature over `entryRef` bind the metadata, so there is no new struct field, no second typehash
(CTR-MTX-11), and `payId` stays unlinkable (CTR-MTX-03). `mtxPayMeta` / `uaPayMeta` publish it in `PaymentMeta`; plain
`mtxPay` with the same id keeps it off chain. Every tier and every non-EVM family (owner 2026-10-26). A new typed
struct with a `meta` field (native wallet display) was rejected: a second struct path and more bytecode in every token.
**Cost if wrong.** Wallets show only the opaque `entryRef`, so a connector that skips the commitment check shows the
user metadata the signature does not bind.
**Source.** `research/mtx-relay-fees.md` §2, §5 (owner answers 2026-10-26: "OK, vậy phần mtxPayMeta như vậy đi").
Change (2026-10-27, controller call, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T7 fix 1): the `meta` body encodings are fixed and family-neutral (one rule for every chain kind) inside `meta = abi.encode(uint16 schema, bytes body)`: schema 1 the raw UTF-8 bytes; schema 2 `abi.encode(string creditorRef, string invoiceNo, uint64 dueDate)`, `dueDate` in Unix seconds; schema 3 `abi.encode(uint256 chainId, bytes32 target, bytes32 callHash)`, `target` as 32 bytes (an EVM address left-padded with zeros, other families their native 32-byte id), `callHash = keccak256(callData)` (research §3); schema 4's inner layout (KEM wrap ‖ AES-256-GCM) stays undefined, a later client item. The shared vectors `smartcontracts/vectors/metatx/paymeta.json` follow them; `long_body_4096` is a hash vector only. Source add: `superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-design.md` §6.1.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27/28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T15): TON only. (1) Pay-meta is the plain `OP_PAY` `SignedOp` with `params = salt:uint256 ^meta` (`meta` as snake bytes): the payer's jetton wallet requires `payRef == metaPayId(salt, meta)`, `lane == payLane(payRef)`, `nonce == 0` (else exit `E_PARAMS` 713; a malformed `params` is TVM's cell underflow 9), emits the external-out `PaymentMeta { master, payId, meta: ^Cell }` (opcode `0x9b1c0d04`) right after `MetaTransactionExecuted`, in the payer wallet's transaction, so it precedes the payee wallet's `PaymentSettled` in logical time, and pays as before; `params = null` is today's `OP_PAY` unchanged. `metaPayId` / `payLane` hash with Tact's `keccak256(Slice)` over the snake chain (each cell's data along its first ref, so the chunking does not matter); getters `get_meta_pay_id(salt, meta)`, `get_pay_lane(p)` on the wallet. (2) The once-set is the payer's own wallet lanes, so once per `(payer, payId)`: another payer's pre-burn of the same `payId` does not block the victim; a plain `OP_PAY` on the same `payRef` / lane shares it (exit `E_NONCE` 706). As every TON lane, the entry lives two `LANE_TTL` windows (30 days each), longer than any op may be valid. (3) Size: no contract cap; measured through a W5R1 lane in @ton/sandbox 0.45.0, 38,100 B (300 snake cells) settles and the 301st cell aborts the emulator whatever the TON attached; config param 43 bounds the lane's external message at 65,535 B and depth 512. The node's `max_pay_meta_bytes` cap (2,048 B) is far below, and `long_body_4096` (4,192 B) also settles on TON. Fees of the payer wallet's transaction at the node's 0.15 TON attach: plain pay 2,792,811 nanoton (27,687 gas); pay-meta 0 B 3,235,545 (32,573), 160 B 3,340,012 (32,760), 2,048 B 4,631,412 (35,527), 4,192 B 6,097,278 (38,663). (4) Adapter (`scaas-node` `ton.rs` `pay_params`): `op.kind` none = plain pay (refused if it carries `extra.params`), `"pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta` hex) checked before any getter, any other kind refused. A TON pay job names no master (the job source keeps the token list, review H1), so the pay-meta job, as every family's, has no token check of its own. (5) The wallet code changed, so every jetton wallet and master address changed: `ton-vectors.json` and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated (test-only chains, no migration).
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27/28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16): TON only, two T15 follow-ups. (1) The wallet refuses a pay-meta whose `meta` is not a plain snake (a cell with more than one ref anywhere along the first-ref chain) with `E_PARAMS` 713 (`common.tact` `requireSnake`): Tact's `keccak256(Slice)` follows only the first ref of each cell, so a second ref would be unsigned yet emitted in `PaymentMeta`. (2) `jetton.spec.ts` › meta size limit asserts only that the largest settling `meta` is ≥ 4,192 B; the binary search runs only with `TON_META_SIZE_SEARCH=1` (the measured 38,100 B = 300 snake cells in @ton/sandbox 0.45.0 stands, entry above). The wallet code changed again, so `ton-vectors.json` and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated (test-only chains).
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T19): client rules from the family builds. TON: a payee wallet bounce leaves `PaymentMeta` emitted without `PaymentSettled` and burns `(payer, payId)` for good, so `PaymentMeta` alone is never proof of payment and a payer signs again with a new salt (T15). Solana: the once-set is the payer's lane PDA, so it lasts until the lane is pruned after `valid_until`; the same `payId` can then be signed and settled again. Aptos (added in the final fix wave, final review M9): the once-set is the payer Account's lane, pruned permissionlessly 30 days after its `valid_until` (`meta::prune`, `PRUNE_DELAY_S`), so it lasts until the prune; the same `payId` can then be signed and settled again. TON (same): the once-set is the payer wallet's lane, which rotates out after one to two `LANE_TTL` (30 days each, `rotateLanes`), so it lasts until the rotation; the same `payId` can then be signed and settled again. On all three a signed payment never replays (`valid_until` bounds it); whether a permanent once-set is wanted instead is on the owner rulings list (final-review.md item 8). Soroban: the once-set is `(from, pay_ref)` (T10 fix 1). The network documents carry the per-family sections (networks/*.md "Pay-meta and relay fee"). Settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (final review owner rulings list item 8): once per (payer, payId) until the lane is pruned / rotated is accepted as family behaviour on Solana, Aptos and TON.

### CTR-MTX-27 — MtxRelayFee: token fee for a fee-less call
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-26 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-27 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner wants a payer to pay, in an mtx token, for a fee-less call such as a PqChat message: the relayer
pays the gas, and the payer pays the relayer. Tender's deposit (CTR-TND-01) already binds a payment to an action
through `entryRef` and the relayer binding. A stateless router generalises it to any target, without token logic in
the target and without changing any token: `ref` commits to (chain, target, call bytes); the payment is bound to the
router as relayer; the router runs the call through an unprivileged executor, then the payment. Owner answers
(2026-10-26): the controller names it and places it in `src/metatx/` with a `DeployBase` CREATE2 deployment; open to
every relayer by default; public balances only; every token tier; non-EVM too (GRAM by escrow); PQ payers sign twice
(option (a), after first picking (c)); no budget mode for now. Rejected: a pay-and-call hook in every token (ERC-1363
style: a new outbound call and bytecode in each token); one combined PQ signature with a transient verified mark
(option (c), studied). CTR-MTX-16's "no generic forwarder" stands: the router grants no authority.
**Cost if wrong.** If the router called targets itself, a `callData` could execute another router-bound payment
through a token, with no call behind it.
**Source.** `research/mtx-relay-fees.md` §3, §5 (owner answers 2026-10-26; "Có, viết spec luôn đi").
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T9 fix 1): (1) the router refuses a target without code, `RelayTargetNoCode(target)`: a counterfactual target (a `SmartKeyAccountFactory` prediction, a CREATE2 clone) relayed before its deploy would succeed as an empty call, pay the fee and burn the lane (against CTR-MTX-13); CTR-MTX-27 gets a ninth conformance item for every family: the target must exist as code / an executable program / an instantiated contract at relay time. (2) `RelayFeePaid.payee` is `bytes32` (a padded address, or the UA id of a derived payee), like `payer`; the other families' events follow this form. (3) The router refuses `t.to == EXECUTOR` (UA: `pad(EXECUTOR)`), and clients never pay or approve the executor. Cost if wrong: a target deployed in the same transaction before the relay is still accepted; a relay cannot pre-pay a target's deploy. Source add: `superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-design.md` §7.1, §7.2.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T10 fix 1): Soroban only. (3) The token's `PayRef` set is keyed by `(from, pay_ref)` for `pay` and `pay_meta`, the per-payer lane of the EVM (`payLane(ref)` in the payer's nonce space), so nobody can pre-burn another payer's `ref` / `payId` with a 0-amount `pay(attacker, attacker, 0, ref, ..)`. (4) The Soroban `relay` takes a payer-signed `salt: BytesN<32>` that enters `ref` (Soroban's call bytes are not unique, the target's auth lives in auth entries): `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ network id ‖ xdr(target) ‖ keccak256(xdr((func, args))) ‖ salt)`, so the same payer can fee-pay two identical calls. (5) Before a relay-fee job the node checks the configured router, a registered token and `amount >= relay_fee.min_amount` (spec §9 names no key; `params.relay_fee = { router, min_amount }`, default 1); the indexer decoding of `PaymentMeta` / `RelayFeePaid` and the `max_pay_meta_bytes` config move to Task 17 for every family. (6) The relayer's `require_auth` is not satisfied by the transaction source alone: the node adds an explicit `SourceAccount` auth entry rooted at the `relay` call.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T11): Solana only. (1) `relay_fee`'s `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ Config.network ‖ target program ‖ keccak256(call) ‖ salt)` with `call = target ‖ u8 n ‖ (pubkey ‖ is_signer ‖ is_writable)×n ‖ data` (the account count added to the spec's preimage so the account list and the data cannot be re-split) and `salt = args.extra`, the payer-signed `MetaOp.extra` (no new argument: a Solana target's own authorisation lives outside its data, so two identical calls need distinct refs). (2) The pay-meta and relay-fee once-set is the payer's lane PDA `[b"lane", Account, lane]`, already per payer: nobody can pre-burn a payer's `payId` / `ref`. (3) New errors `PayMetaShape` (pay-meta `pay_ref` / lane / nonce mismatch), `RelayFeeShape`, `RelayTargetNoCode` (the target is not an executable program). (4) Open mode pays the lane's ATA directly, so `PaymentSettled.to` and `RelayFeePaid.payee` name the lane (no hop through the marker, which never holds tokens and never signs). (5) No executor: `scaas` invokes the target with plain `invoke` (no PDA signer seeds). Because `invoke` forwards the outer transaction's signer privileges, `relay_fee` refuses on chain (`RelayFeeShape`, before the CPI) any target account flagged signer, the lane or any co-signer, so the router grants no authority to whichever relayer submits it (CTR-MTX-16; T11 fix 1). The node refuses the same, and the lane as a target account, before simulating. Cost if wrong: a target that needs a signer (a rent payer) cannot be fee-relayed through the generic `relay_fee`.
Change (2026-10-27, owner 2026-10-27; status: current; commit: metatx-split T11 fix 2): owner 2026-10-27: Solana uses static relay_fee_<entry> wrappers (as Sui/Aptos); generic CPI relay_fee kept for external programs. Wrapped: `manage_signed`, `mandate_open`, `mandate_revoke_signed`, `mandate_close_signed`, `cancel_signed`, `invalidate_nonces_signed` (every fee-less signed entry of `scaas` but `open_passkey`, excluded as a scope choice: account creation is not among the entries Sui / Aptos wrap, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; `settle` is a trade with its own market fee and the pay entries are payments). Each runs the entry's body in-process, then the router payment (marker as relayer, open mode pays the lane), atomically. `ref` uses the Solana preimage with target = `scaas` and `call` = the entry's instruction as if sent alone (declared accounts with their flags, `discriminator ‖ Borsh(arguments)`, its `auth` included), salt `args.extra`. To nest beside any entry's accounts, `RelayPay` no longer reads instruction arguments (`subject` and `lane_pda` are derived, checked and the lane PDA created in the shared body); `manage_signed` persists its Account before returning so a wrapper's payment reads the new key set. The self-target refusal of the generic `relay_fee` stays. Settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 5): the generic CPI `relay_fee` for external programs is kept next to the static wrappers.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T11 fix 3): the wrapper ref hashes the router marker in the lane slot (lane-agnostic, as Sui/Aptos): `call`'s first account (the inner entry's `lane`, flags as declared) is the marker PDA `[b"relayfee"]`, so the payer signs before any lane is known, open mode stays open to every relayer, and a job moved to another lane still settles. Cost if wrong: none found; the lane is still the transaction's signer and the entry's rent payer.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T12): Cosmos only. (1) `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ chain id bytes ‖ target (canonical address bytes, 32 for a contract) ‖ keccak256(msg))`, `msg` the exact bytes the executor sends; no salt: the target sees the unprivileged `relayexec` and no funds, so nothing outside `msg` authorises the call, and the SCaaS fee-less signed entries carry their signature and nonce / once-ref inside `msg` (token `Relay` / `RelayPayMeta`, mandate `PayUnderMandate`, DEX `Settle`); the entries authorised by `info.sender` (mandate `Revoke` / `Withdraw`, DEX admin) fail through the router, so nothing is paid. (2) The router refuses a target without contract info (`relayfee: target is not an instantiated contract`), `op.to == executor`, and non-empty funds; the executor refuses funds and every caller but its router. (3) Re-entry into the router is refused by a stored flag set in `Relay` and cleared in the reply of its last message (CTR-MTX-27 conformance; CosmWasm allows re-entry). (4) The router computes its executor's address with `instantiate2_address(code checksum, router, "scaas.relayexec")` at instantiate (its one stored item besides the flag). (5) `relay_fee_paid` (`ref`, `target`, `token`, `payer`, `payee`, `amount`, bech32 `Addr`s) is the router's own event, so wasmd lists it before the sub-messages' events; it exists only when the whole transaction succeeded. (6) The token's lanes are already per payer (`NONCES[(from, lane)]`), so `RelayPayMeta` and the router payment are once per `(payer, payId / ref)` and an attacker's 0-amount pay of the same id uses its own lane. (7) Node: `op.kind = "pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta`) builds `relay_pay_meta`; `op.kind = "relay_fee"` (`op.contract` = `params.relay_fee.router`, `op.extra.target`, `op.extra.msg` hex) builds the router's `Relay` after the policy, ref, lane, nonce and relayer checks; a `params.relay_fee.router` that is set but is not a lowercase 32-byte contract address of the chain's prefix is a startup error.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T12 fix 1): Cosmos only. (1) The router and the executor have no admin: a migrated router is the bound relayer of every payment signed to it and could settle one without running the call (CTR-MTX-13). `Relay` queries the router's own `ContractInfo` and refuses while `admin` is set (`relayfee: the router has an admin`; a failed query fails closed); the executor is instantiated with `admin: None`; deploy tooling instantiates `relayfee` with `--no-admin`; clients check `ContractInfo.admin == None` before signing `relayer = router`. (2) The router as its own target is refused by the re-entry flag. (3) A `params.relay_fee.min_amount` that is not a non-negative integer is a node startup error, like an unparsable `router`. (4) `build-wasm.sh` links with `-C link-arg=--allow-undefined` (cosmwasm-std 3.0.10 declares its host imports without `wasm_import_module = "env"`, and newer rustc no longer passes the flag) and then fails unless every wasm import is a cosmwasm-std `env` host function (`cosmwasm-check` when installed, else a stdlib import-section parser).
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T13): Sui only. (1) `meta::relay_pay_meta` derives `pay_ref = meta_pay_id(salt, meta)`, `lane = pay_lane(pay_ref)`, `nonce = 0` on chain and runs `relay_pay`'s body (a private `settle` shared with `relay_pay` and `pay_routed`), emitting `PaymentMeta` before `PaymentSettled`; the once-set is the payer's own `Account.lanes`, so once per `(payer, payId)` and another payer's pay of the same id uses its own table. (2) `scaas::relayfee` has one static wrapper per fee-less signed entry (`relay_manage`, `relay_revoke_with_sig`, `relay_cancel`, `relay_invalidate_nonces`); each runs the entry, then `meta::pay_routed` (`public(package)`), which fixes `pay_ref = ref`, `lane = pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce = 0`, `relayer = marker` on chain, so a payment settles only for the call it was signed for; `dex::cancel`'s `false` aborts the relay (`ECallRefused`). (3) `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ network ‖ original package id ‖ keccak256(call) ‖ salt)`, `call` = BCS of the entry's name and every argument (objects as ids, the entry's `Auth` included), `salt` = the payment's payer-signed `extra`; no sender and no lane, so any relayer may submit. (4) Marker = the shared `RelayFee` object (created in `init`); plain `relay_pay` / `relay_pay_meta` refuse a payment bound to it (`EWrongRelayer`: no sender is an object); open mode pays `ctx.sender()`, the marker is never paid. (5) manage / cancel / invalidate pay from the account the entry names (Move allows one `&mut` per object in a PTB command); paying another coin or another payer's account for these needs a further wrapper variant (not built). (6) Upgrade authority: `relayfee` is a module of the `scaas` package, so it shares the token's `UpgradeCap` and cannot be upgraded separately; the router's trust equals the token's, so no code change. NET-SUI-15 (immutable package) is still SPECIFIED; as built the publisher keeps the `UpgradeCap`. (7) Node: `op.kind = "pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta`) builds `relay_pay_meta`; `op.kind = "relay_fee"` (`op.extra.call` = the call bytes, `op.extra.registry`, `op.extra.mandate_coin_type` for revoke) builds `relayfee::relay_<entry>` after the checks: payment relayer = `params.relay_fee.router` (the `RelayFee` id), registry registered and the paying account derived from it and the payer, `amount ≥ min_amount`, canonical call bytes of a wrapped entry naming the paying account, `pay_ref == ref`, `lane == pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce == 0`; an unparsable `router` or `min_amount` is a startup error. (8) Fix 1 (controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; commit: metatx-split T13 fix 1): `RelayFee` exists only if `relayfee` is in the package's first publish (Sui runs no `init` for a module added by an upgrade); for manage / cancel / invalidate the payer is the call's own account, so a sponsor needs `_from` variants (not built); the node refuses a plain pay / pay-meta whose `to` is the configured router marker, and a malformed `tokens[].address` is a startup error. Item (6) settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 9): the package is made immutable at deploy (`deploy.sh sui` destroys the `UpgradeCap`), so nobody can upgrade token or router.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T14): Aptos only. (1) `meta::relay_pay_meta` (`package entry`) derives `pay_ref = meta_pay_id(salt, meta)`, `lane = pay_lane(pay_ref)`, `nonce = 0` on chain and runs `relay_pay`'s body (a private `settle` shared with `relay_pay` and `pay_routed`), emitting `PaymentMeta` before `PaymentSettled`; the view `pay_meta_check` is its `pay_check` twin; the once-set is the payer's own `Account.lanes`, so once per `(payer, payId)`. (2) `scaas::relayfee` has one `package entry` wrapper per fee-less signed entry (`relay_manage_signed`, `relay_mandate_open`, `relay_revoke_signed`, `relay_cancel_signed`, `relay_invalidate_nonces_signed`); each runs the entry, then `meta::pay_routed` (`package`), which fixes `pay_ref = ref`, `lane = pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce = 0`, `relayer = marker` on chain; `dex::cancel_signed`'s body moved to `package fun dex::cancel(…): bool` and a `false` (order already closed) aborts the relay (`ECALL_REFUSED`). (3) `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ chain_id (1 byte) ‖ @scaas ‖ keccak256(call) ‖ salt)`: Aptos's `MetaOp` domain carries a `u8` chain id, not network bytes, so `chain` is that byte; `call` = BCS of the entry's name and every argument (signature included, lane signer excluded), `salt` = the payment's payer-signed `extra`; no sender, no lane. (4) Marker = `object::create_object_address(&@scaas, b"scaas.relayfee")`, a derived address no transaction can sign for: plain `relay_pay` / `relay_pay_meta` refuse a payment bound to it (`EWRONG_RELAYER`); open mode pays the lane; the marker is never paid; nothing is stored, so `relayfee` needs no `init_module`. (5) Any Account pays (no Sui-style one-account limit). (6) Upgrade authority: `relayfee` is a module of the `scaas` package, so the code object's owner can upgrade it only together with `meta`; the router's trust equals the token's, so no code change; NET-APT-20 (immutable) is still SPECIFIED, as built `upgrade_policy = "compatible"`. (7) Node: `op.kind = "pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta`) builds `relay_pay_meta` (or calls `pay_meta_check` while the Account is not open); `op.kind = "relay_fee"` (`op.extra.call` = the call bytes, optional `op.ref`) builds `relayfee::relay_<entry>` after the checks: payment relayer = `params.relay_fee.router`, which must equal `relayfee::marker()` of the package (else a startup error), the asset a registered token, `amount ≥ min_amount`, canonical call bytes of a wrapped entry, `pay_ref == ref`, `lane == pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce == 0`; a plain pay / pay-meta to the marker is refused; a relay-fee job whose payer's Account is not open is refused (simulation cannot run it); a malformed `tokens[].address` or `min_amount` is a startup error. (8) Fix 1 (controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; commit: metatx-split T14 fix 1): the Aptos node refuses a plain pay / pay-meta to `relayfee::marker()` of the package whether or not a router is configured (the marker is derived, so it is always known); on Aptos and Sui an unknown `op.kind` is refused (only none = plain pay, `pay_meta`, `relay_fee`), so a typo never burns the `(payer, payId)` lane as a plain pay without publishing `meta`. Item (6) settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 9): `upgrade_policy = "immutable"`, so nobody can upgrade `relayfee` or `meta`.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27/28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16): TON only (spec §7.2 TON row). (1) Escrow, not a call: `ScaasRelayFee` (`relayfee.tact`) takes `RelayCall { target, call, salt, payWallet, payOp, payAuth, payStateInit?, master, deadline }`, recomputes `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ global id:int32 ‖ target wc:int8 ‖ target hash ‖ cellHash(call) ‖ salt)` (the representation hash covers every ref of `call`; `salt` is payer-chosen and signed through `payRef`; no sender or lane, any relayer may submit), checks the router-bound `OP_PAY` (`payRef == ref`, `lane == payLane(ref)`, `nonce == 0`, `relayer == to == router`, `amount > 0`, `payWallet == walletAddress(from, master)`; exit 741), escrows it under `(from, ref)` (742 while pending or while that payer wallet has a payment in flight) and sends the payer wallet the `SignedOp` with `params = null`. (2) Provable success: a one-shot `RelayExecutor` (per router, payer, salt; the target sees it, never the router) sends the call and right after it a bounceable `RelayProbe`; TON's in-order delivery per account pair makes the probe's bounce, with no call bounce before it, the proof the call ran → release to the relayer and `RelayFeePaid` (`0x9b1c0d05`); the call's bounce (also: a target with no account) → refund. The call carries at least config param 21's `gas_limit` priced by `getComputeFee` + 0.02 TON, so a failed call can always bounce (no silent failure). This replaces the brief's "release on the target's excess": an excess can be forged by any transfer to the target that names the router as response destination. (3) Timeout: `deadline` in `(now, now + 3,600 s]` (743); anyone's `RelayRefund { from, ref }` at or after it refunds a funded escrow or drops an unfunded one (745 before, 744 unknown). Release and refund delete the escrow first: exclusive; a late report pays nothing; the router holds no jetton after settlement (tested) and its TON moves by < 0.001 TON per relay. Refund wins whenever success is not provable (a target that accepts the probe). (4) Per payer: escrow keys and the payer's wallet lane are per `(payer, ref)`, so a copied `ref` paid first by an attacker is its own escrow and the victim's relay still settles (tested); the brief's "one pending call per target" is not built (the executor makes the outcome attributable without it). (5) Notifications other than the escrow's own (a plain transfer, a payment whose escrow timed out, a foreign wallet) are handed back to the notifying wallet's sender; R18: a `call` that is a `SignedOp` / `MandatePay` naming the router as relayer is refused (707), and so is the probe opcode. (6) No admin and no upgrade path: the router's and the executor's code are fixed at deploy. (7) Adapter (`ton.rs`): `op.kind = "relay_fee"` checked before any getter (router = `params.relay_fee.router`, startup error if unparsable; master in the chain's `tokens`; `amount >= min_amount`, default 1, non-integer = startup error; the binding to `(target, call, salt)`), then the payer wallet derivation, the signature simulation and `get_relay_value`; deadline = now + 600 s. `tx_status` follows the escrow (`get_escrow_state`): pending while open, mined once `RelayFeePaid` of the ref is seen, reverted when refunded; past `deadline` the lane sends `RelayRefund` (retried every 120 s). A plain pay to the router and a present but non-string `op.kind` are refused. Measured (sandbox): `get_relay_value` 306,666,673 nanoton; release 15 transactions, 16,684,899 nanoton fees; refund 15 transactions, 15,540,542.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner delegated "choose the best option"; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16 fix 1): TON only, supersedes items (2) and (5) of the T16 entry above. (1) Release only on a positive acknowledgment from a known SCaaS target. The review reproduced that a call whose action phase fails gets no bounce (only sends with mode +16 bounce on action failure), rolls its state back, and still let the probe bounce, so the T16 rule "probe bounce without a call bounce = success" released the fee for a call that did not happen. Now: the router serves only targets whose `RelayCall.targetInit` derives the target and whose code hash is the SCaaS jetton wallet's or the Mandate's (compiled into the router), and only their fee-less entries (wallet `set_key` / `revoke`, Mandate owner `revoke`); each sends `RelayAck { digest }` to its sender as its last message before the excess, and a failed action phase sends no message at all; the executor releases iff the ack (sender = target, digest = the call's MetaOp) arrives before the probe's bounce, refunds on a probe bounce without one or on the call's bounce, and the timeout refunds. The ack echoes the executed MetaOp's digest, not the executor's lt as the ruling sketched: the target cannot know the lt, and the digest binds the ack to this very call (the executor sends nothing else that acks). (2) The call's `SignedOp.responseDestination` must be the payer's executor (on chain, 741), so a payer-chosen target cannot keep the relayer's call TON (review important 1), and a copied `ref` cannot be relayed by another payer. The node also prices the exposure: a relay-fee job's fee × `params.relay_fee.min_ton_value[master]` (nanoton per base unit; no price feed exists) must reach the `get_relay_value` the lane sends, else the job is refused (spec §9). (3) Every TON amount is priced at run time: `getComputeFee` of fixed gas units (×2 the measured use), `getForwardFee` of each message's `computeDataSize`, `getStorageFee` for the router's rent; the call is sent with `SendPayFwdFeesSeparately` and carries `max(config param 21's gas_limit priced + its bounce, the served entry's own floor: the wallet's 0.05 TON, the Mandate's 0.1 TON)`; `get_relay_value(body)` and `get_refund_value` replace the fixed constants (review important 2). (4) Settlement transfers carry a `queryId` (a ring of the last 16); a bounce from the router's wallet restores the escrow as release-owed / refund-owed and any `RelayRefund` sends it again at any time; `RelayRefund` needs `get_refund_value` (714 below; review important 3). (5) The node identifies a closed escrow positively by the router's `RelayFeePaid` / new `RelayFeeRefunded { ref, payer, amount }` (`0x9b1c0d06`, also emitted with amount 0 when an unfunded entry is dropped) of this `(payer, ref)`; neither seen = pending, never "refunded" by absence (review important 4). (6) The router reserves its prior balance in every handler and keeps each escrow's rent from the relay, so it never pays for relays and never freezes (minor 3). (7) Recorded (minor 1): one payment of a payer wallet in flight at a time; a griefer can hold that slot for one round trip per spam (garbage auth bounces quickly): liveness only. (8) Recorded (minor 2): a served target always refuses the probe, so a swallowed probe (executor dust waiting for a timeout) does not happen with the served code set; the dust of a probe that bounces after a call bounce stays in the executor (≈ 0.001 TON). (9) Recorded (minor 4): success = the target's handling transaction was acknowledged; the messages it sends on (a revoke's cancel to the DEX) are not covered. Measured (sandbox, @ton/sandbox 0.45.0): `get_relay_value` 167,085,766 nanoton; release 16 transactions, 24,900,308 nanoton fees; refund 15 transactions, 23,524,374. The wallet and Mandate code changed (the ack), so `ton-vectors.json` and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated. (10) Recorded residual (final review M8, recorded in the metatx-split final fix wave): the settlement ring of (4) keeps the last `SETTLE_RING = 16` settlements (`relayfee.tact:106`, `settle`); more than 16 settlements between a settlement's send and its bounce evict the entry, the bounce is then ignored and the tokens stay in the router's jetton wallet with no admin to recover them. Rare: only an underfunded settlement bounces, and the bounce arrives in the next transaction (networks/ton.md). Scope settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 4): only the SCaaS jetton wallet's set_key / revoke and the Mandate owner revoke, open mode only, a 3,600 s timeout, no third-party targets.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16 fix 2): TON only. (1) A signed revoke runs at most once (NET-TON-18, BUILT): the wallet accepted `next == nonce` or `next == nonce + 1` for a revoke and set `next + 1`, so a revoke that ran in its first form (the order never left: `next == nonce`) could be replayed by anyone in the second form, spending `nonce + 1` and sending a `CancelTag` (reproduced through the relay router, where the replay was also released). Every revoke now leaves its lane at `nonce + 2`; the fix is in the wallet, so the direct (non-relayed) path is fixed too; the Mandate's owner revoke checks its lane exactly (`used == nonce`) and had no such replay. (2) Node attribution: `RelayFeeRefunded` gains `relayer` (the escrow's), and the node counts only events of its own relay: `RelayFeePaid` with `payee` = its lane, `RelayFeeRefunded` with `relayer` = its lane, a release winning over a refund of the same `(payer, ref)` (paid at most once; a refund of ours next to it is an earlier attempt). So a third party's copied `RelayCall` after a release (refunded with amount 0 to its own relayer) and another relayer's release are never reported as ours; our own amount-0 refund (our payment refused or dropped) still closes our job, which ignoring all amount-0 events would have left pending forever. The router does not refuse a settled `(payer, ref)`: the payer wallet's lane does (the copy bounces at nonce 0). (3) TON that reaches the executor after its report (a revoke-cancel's excess, about 0.36 TON in the review's run) goes on to the relayer (`RelayExec.relayer`); a revoke-cancel's call carries `MIN_SIGNED_OP_TON + forwardTon` at least, so it is not under-funded. (4) The settlement ring keeps the escrow without its `call` (rent). (5) Wording: the ack goes just before the entry's own outgoing message (the excess, or a revoke's cancel transfer), not always before the excess. The wallet code changed, so `ton-vectors.json` (now with the event layouts) and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated.
Change (2026-10-28, controller rulings 2026-10-27/28 widening Task 17, owner may override; status: current; commits: metatx-split T17a 9777679f, T17b 1683d2ac, T17c 3a98e74a, T17d 399e9e77, T17e ea3a0330, T17f d784f264): the node (`scaas-node`), every family. (A) `guard::ERC1271_FLOOR` = 21,000 + (400,000 · 64/63 + 5,000) · 64/63 + `ERC1271_PREFIX` = 467,904: the ERC-1271 call of a `SmartKeyAccount` signer now runs two frames below the token (token → `MtxPipelineLib` → wallet); `ERC1271_PREFIX` = 29,026 is forge's measured minimum relayer call gas of a `SmartKeyAccount`-signed `mtxExecute` (446,904, `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-node-floor.txt`, Task 8) minus the two-frame term (417,878); calldata gas still comes from the simulation (+20 %); pinned by `erc1271_floor_covers_forge_minimum` (reads the log). (B) One config key set for every family: `params.relay_fee = { router, min_amount (default 1), relay_bound_payee (default false), min_ton_value (TON), min_lamports_value (Solana) }` and `params.max_pay_meta_bytes` (default 2,048), read by `ChainCfg::relay_params` and checked in `Config::validate`; a set-but-invalid value (an unparsable router in the family's address form, a non-integer or negative amount, a non-integer cap, a non-boolean flag) is a startup error in every adapter (Soroban fell back to `min_amount` 1 and dropped an unparsable router; Solana clamped a negative amount). (C) One `op.kind` rule (`adapter::op_kind`): absent / null = the plain pay, `pay_meta` / `relay_fee` (Solana's wrappers ride `relay_fee` with `extra.entry`) = those, any other string or a present non-string (`7`, `true`, `{}`) is refused, and a kind-less job carrying `salt` / `meta` is refused; EVM and Hedera jobs: `kind` absent, `metatx` or `call`. (D) Never a plain pay or pay-meta to the router, marker or executor: EVM (router, executor = the router's first `CREATE`, `router.create(1)`), Soroban (router), Solana (the marker PDA and the program id), Cosmos (router and its `relayexec`, read once with `QueryMsg::Executor`); Sui, Aptos, TON as before. (E) A relay-fee job is relayed only when the fee reaches the node's lane (open mode, or a payee bound to the lane) and is at least `min_amount`; a fee bound to anyone else is refused unless `relay_bound_payee = true`, and then counts as sponsored (no `min_amount`); TON relays are always open (the escrow releases to the relaying lane). (F) The fee covers what the adapter can price: `amount >= min_amount` everywhere (the operator's price of the gas; no token price feed, no gas price or block limit assumed); Solana: when the payment's `LanePda` (56 B) does not exist yet and the fee is the node's, `amount × min_lamports_value[mint]` must reach its rent-exempt minimum (`getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption`), and a mint without a price gets no such job; TON: `min_ton_value` (T16). Not priced (recorded): a first-use recipient ATA or a lazily opened Account on Solana; Soroban / Sui / Aptos storage and rent are inside the simulated fee. (G) The indexer of every family decodes `PaymentMeta` and `RelayFeePaid` and joins them (`indexer::join_pay_events`): only the expected token's `PaymentSettled` proves a payment; a `PaymentMeta` gives its `meta` to the next `PaymentSettled` of the same token, transaction and payId (and `from` where the event names one); a `RelayFeePaid` from the configured router gives `relay_target` / `relay_payee` to its token's `PaymentSettled` with the same `(from, ref)`, amount and payee (or the router, open mode); never by id alone; neither is sent as a row of its own, because the client's `chain_event_ingest` (the ERP side) accepts only `PaymentSettled`, `MetaTransactionExecuted` and `Transfer` and reads new keys only as fields (`meta`, `relay_target`, `relay_payee`). TON: `PaymentMeta` has no `from`, so it takes the payer from the same transaction's authenticated `Executed` and waits (in memory, bounded by 10,000 masterchain blocks; a restart drops the wait, the payment then reaches the client without `meta`) for the later `PaymentSettled` of the same `(master, from, pay_ref)`; a meta cell with more than one ref is refused by the decoder; `RelayFeePaid` / `RelayFeeRefunded` stay with `tx_status` (the outcome scan of the last 128 router transactions, `Pending` when unseen): their release or refund lands after the escrow's `PaymentSettled` already reached the client, so the indexer cannot attach them. (H) The regenerated DEX KAT (Task 4) passes in `clients/clientkeys` (107 pass, 2 skipped) and `scaas-node` (337 lib tests, EVM e2e 4/4, the e2e harness on Amsterdam anvil as main 123e947f). The EVM node has no UA job path, so `uaPayMeta` / `uaRelay` are not served (a later item). Cost if wrong: a stricter node (refused kinds, refused bound payees) turns jobs away that a looser rule would have relayed; operators set `relay_bound_payee` / `min_lamports_value` to widen it. Settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28: the flat `params.relay_fee.min_amount` (default 1 base unit, per chain) is kept until before mainnet, then re-decided (item 7, TODO); the TON outcome window (`tx_status`, the last 128 router transactions; an older job stays Pending) is accepted (item 11).
Change (2026-10-28, controller calls 2026-10-28 on the owner's delegation "choose the best option"; status: current; commit: metatx-split T17 fix 1): supersedes items (A) and the TON wait of (G) above, and tightens (B). (A) The floor a contract signer's meta-tx gets is per job: `guard::erc1271_floor(len)` = 21,000 + 64 gas per calldata byte (the EIP-7976 floor rate) + `ERC1271_CALL_GAS` (446,904, forge's minimum relayer CALL gas, which counts no intrinsic and no calldata) + 10 % of it (512,594 at zero calldata); an anvil e2e sends a `SmartKeyAccount`-signed `mtxExecute` with exactly that gas and it settles. (G) TON: the `PaymentMeta` wait is looked up, never taken, so a range that fails after the join and is read again still carries `meta` (the `(master, from, payId)` triple happens once on chain); entries leave by expiry (10,000 masterchain blocks) or, past 4,096, oldest first with a warning; the wait is written atomically to `params.meta_journal` (default: `<store dir>/ton-meta-<chain>.json`) and loaded at start, so a restart keeps it. (B) A `params.relay_fee` key outside `router`, `min_amount`, `relay_bound_payee` and the family's own price key (`min_ton_value` on TON, `min_lamports_value` on Solana) is a startup error naming the key; Solana and Soroban refuse a malformed `tokens[].address` at start (as Sui, Aptos, TON); Solana refuses a `router` that is not its program id; Cosmos reads the router's executor lazily, once, on the first job that needs it (a relay-fee job, or a pay to a 32-byte contract address), and retries only such jobs until it answers, so a down router never stalls plain pays (T17 fix 2). The TON meta journal is written to a temporary file, synced, then renamed; over the cap, entries whose payment was already seen leave before still-waiting ones (T17 fix 2). Recorded, not built: the EVM node's UA path (`uaPayMeta`, `uaRelay`, the `UAPaymentSettled` join) is a new feature (TODO.md); TON `RelayFeePaid` / `RelayFeeRefunded` stay with `tx_status` (`Pending` when unseen), accepted. Cost if wrong: a contract signer's job pays for up to 10 % more gas limit than it uses.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T19): rules and records from the family builds, in full. (1) Solana `cancel_signed` and `mandate_revoke_signed` are idempotent: a front-run of the signed entry still lets the wrapper run and the payer pays its signed fee once (superseded by owner ruling 2026-10-28, item 6 of the final review's owner rulings list: the wrappers refuse a no-op, `RelayCallNoOp`, see the owner-rulings Change below); a passkey x passkey wrapper transaction against the 4,096-byte v1 limit is untested and fails closed. (3) TON: a client does not queue an op at `n + 1` behind a revocable order at `n` (a signed revoke leaves its lane at `n + 2`); a racing other relayer's release makes our amount-0 refund path report "payer not charged" though the other relayer charged the payer (low, recorded). Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current, done; commits: metatx-split T10 fix 1 `351f67ea` (Soroban), T11–T16 (each family's adapter), T17 `9777679f`..`d784f264`; standalone line added in the final fix wave, final review M7): every family, one rule. The spec §9 node checks of a pay-meta or relay-fee job (configured router, registered token, `amount >= relay_fee.min_amount`, the binding of the payment to the call) go into each family's own adapter task (T10–T16), not into one node task; the indexer decoding of `PaymentMeta` / `RelayFeePaid` and the `max_pay_meta_bytes` config move to Task 17 for every family. Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28 on final review I1, owner may override; status: current, its residuals superseded by the re-review Change below; commit: metatx-split final fix wave `deead173`): TON only, node. Before it sends a `RelayCall` the node checks the relayed call against its target with getters, as it checks the payment (`check_relayed_call` in `scaas-node/src/adapters/ton.rs`), and refuses the job with `RELAY_CALL_REFUSED`. Every other family simulates the whole relay; on TON a failing call bounced after the payment settled, the escrow refunded the payer and the relayer paid the bounce (about 0.025 TON in the sandbox, `runs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-ton.txt:143`), repeatable at no cost to the submitter. Checks: the call's `contract`, network and `from` are the target, this chain and the target's owner (the first field of its StateInit data); it is valid past the relay's `deadline`; its `relayer` is none or the call's `responseDestination` (the router checks that this is the executor). Jetton wallet target: `simulate_signed` as for any signed op (lane nonce incl. a revoke at n + 1; the bound key or the StateInit key; the TON Connect signature), `valid_until <= now + LANE_TTL`, a set_key's `params` hashing to `extra` and never by passkey, a cancel's forward >= `CANCEL_TON`. Mandate target: an owner revoke only, TON Connect-signed, the Mandate not yet revoked, the signature verified against `get_state`'s `ownerPubkey`. The residuals first recorded here (a passkey's P-256 signature unchecked; no Mandate lane-nonce getter) were wrong to call owner-limited (any submitter owns a wallet, and a passkey call needs no key at all) and are closed by the re-review Change below. Not built (optional in the review): a per-payer failure budget and the payer's jetton balance check. Test: `ton_relay_fee_refuses_failing_call_before_send` (RED before the check: a wrongly signed call built). The meta journal also syncs its directory after the rename (final review M13).
Change (2026-10-28, controller calls 2026-10-28 on the fix-wave re-review F1 / F2 / m2–m4, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split final fix wave re-review fixes `6c31fbac`): TON only, node and Mandate. (F1) The node refuses a passkey-signed relayed call on the jetton wallet (`RELAY_CALL_REFUSED`, "a passkey-signed call is not relayed") until it can verify P-256: any submitter could otherwise relay a passkey revoke with a garbage signature at the relayer's cost. Passkey users on TON cannot use the relay-fee router meanwhile; they send revoke / set_key directly. Cost if wrong: passkey users lose the gasless revoke / set_key until P-256 lands in the node (`p256` dependency, owner's call). (F2a) A set_key with `extra != 0` must carry `params` that hash to `extra` and are laid out as the wallet parses a passkey record (exactly 520 bits and one ref, `jetton.tact` set_key); a malformed record bounced without spending the lane, repeatable. (F2b) The call's `responseDestination` must equal the router's `get_executor(payer, salt)`; a mismatch made the router throw 741 after the relayer paid its gas and forward fees. (F2c) The TON Mandate gains `get fun get_lane_nonce(lane)` (its owner lanes never rotate; a contract change, all chains test-only, no migration; the router address and `ton-vectors.json` `relay_fee` router / pay-op / RelayCall vectors moved with the Mandate code hash, regenerated); the node refuses a Mandate revoke whose nonce is not the lane's next. (m2) A revoke of an already revoked Mandate would run and change nothing: the node refuses it as a no-op, so the payer does not pay for nothing (owner rulings list item 6), not because it would fail. (m3) The call's validity floor is documented: `valid_until` later than the relay's deadline, now + 600 s (`RELAY_DEADLINE_S`). (m4) A target code that is neither the wallet's nor the Mandate's (`get_codes` on the router) is refused at once instead of retried as a transport error. (P1, second re-review, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split final fix wave second re-review `f0d4025e`) The payment leg is checked as the payer's wallet runs it: valid at most `LANE_TTL` ahead (`E_TTL`) and within the payer wallet's `get_wallet_data` balance (`E_BALANCE`), else the job is refused before anything is sent; a plain pay has the same two gaps at one hop's cost, left to the fee policy (owner rulings list item 7). Remaining exposure, recorded: a race in which the owner spends the lane, or moves its tokens away, between the check and the message's arrival still bounces at the relayer's cost, but costs the submitter a direct op or a paid relay each time; two relay-fee jobs of one payer wallet within one payment round trip make the router refuse the second (742) after the relayer paid its forward fee; every burst of such failures rides on one paid relay of the submitter, so the node does not hold the second job (an adapter-level per-payer-wallet hold is possible but not built, controller call); no per-payer failure budget is built (owner's call). Test: `ton_relay_fee_refuses_failing_payment_before_send`. (Q1, controller call 2026-10-28, then owner ruling 2026-10-28: risk acceptance reversed, fix kept; status: current; commits: metatx-split final fix wave third re-review `07d2f411`, removed by `2cac867a` under the owner's first answer, restored by its revert `0c90f031`) The payment gets the call's validity floor: it must stay valid more than 600 s (`RELAY_DEADLINE_S`), since the payer's wallet sees it two hops after the lane (`E_EXPIRED` would bounce at the relayer's cost, repeatable), and the lane transaction expires at `min(valid_until − 300 s, deadline)`, so a late lane transaction never delivers a nearly expired payment; a plain pay has the same window, left to the fee policy (owner rulings list item 7), no code. A balance equal to the amount pays (tested). Tests: `ton_relay_fee_refuses_failing_call_before_send` (every check has a case that fails without it, mutation-checked), jest `mandate.spec.ts` (`get_lane_nonce`).

Change (2026-10-28, owner ruling 2026-10-28 on the final review's owner rulings list item 1; status: **superseded 2026-10-30** by owner rulings D1 (signatures) and D2 (callers), CTR-MTX-25 / CTR-MTX-18 / CTR-UA-24 changes of 2026-10-30, built on `no7702` `5ddc577d` / `6bb05818`; commit: metatx-split owner rulings `84b0a469`): EIP-7702 delegate-only signatures are accepted on both paths. The address path (`SigCheck.isValid`: `MetaTxBase` / `MtxPipelineLib` `mtxExecute` and the transfers, `SCaaSDex` orders and cancels, `MandateWallet`, `SmartKeyAccount`) follows accounts.md CTR-UA-24, one rule with the UA path: empty code ⇒ ECDSA low-s by the address; code exactly the designator `0xef0100 ‖ address` ⇒ ECDSA by the address accepted, otherwise ERC-1271 on the address (it runs the delegate) under the 50 k cap (400 k for `SmartKeyAccount` clones); other code ⇒ ERC-1271. `SigCheck.isValid7702` is folded into `isValid`. The node's DEX venue mirrors it (`valid_sig`); the node's ERC-1271 gas floor already applies to a 7702 `from` (`has_code` is true for a designator). Follow-up `12039013`: `SCaaSDex` grew 45 B, so the DEX KAT's clone address and DEX-domain digests moved (`dex_order_kat.json` regenerated, clientkeys and scaas-node re-gated green); `test_7702_nativeFrom` now expects the address-path delegate signature to pass.
Change (2026-10-30, controller call 2026-10-28 and owner ruling 2026-10-28 item 10 "the EVM node's UA path after the merge"; choices made by the node-ua-jobs build, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs `f0f8fd50`): the EVM node relays the `ua_metatx` job kind (job-api.md), with `uaPayMeta`, `MtxRelayFee.uaRelay` and the `UAPaymentSettled` join. (1) Payload as job-api.md specifies, `{token, struct, m, auth}`; `m` keeps the address structs' wire field names with `from` / `to` as bytes32 ids; a `ua_metatx` job carrying `metatx`, `signature`, `entry` or `call` is refused, a `metatx` job never carries a UA body. (2) `uaPayMeta` is no new kind: a `ua_metatx` job with `struct = transfer` and `salt` / `meta`, the address pay-meta checks on ids before any simulation (`entryRef = metaPayId(salt, meta)`, `batch = payLane(entryRef)`, nonce 0, `max_pay_meta_bytes`), an off-chain meta relays the plain `uaExecuteTransfer`. (3) `uaRelay` is a `call` job with its own call-table row `MtxRelayFee.uaRelay` (rule `RelayFee`), as `relay` is: the router's shape on ids (payee never `pad(executor)`, open mode `t.to = pad(router)`), `min_amount` and `relay_bound_payee` unchanged. (4) A `ua_metatx` job runs only on a registered token whose UA ledger is on (`registry() ≠ 0`, cached once true; else `FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED`): `uaExecute*` exists only on the token's UA ledger until UA-5c (c)(d) puts the generic UA pipeline into `MetaTxBase` / `MandateWallet`. (5) No pre-simulation UA allowlist check: tokens publish no UA selector table (`mtxSelectors()` is the address allowlist), so the selector, the fee class, the kind and the registration of `from` are answered by the simulation of the exact call; the gateway's record cache and local verify of cheap kinds (`UA_NOT_REGISTERED` at intake, gateway.md) are not built. (6) The relayer never loses on a relay fee (owner rule): after the simulation the fee × `params.relay_fee.min_wei_value[token]` (wei per base unit; EVM only; token-address keys, an integer or a decimal string, anything else a startup error) must reach the quote = the gas limit × the max fee per gas the lane signs with (the same fees then sign it), else `RELAY_FEE_REFUSED` and nothing is signed; as NEAR `min_yocto_value` and Algorand `min_microalgo_value`. Required for `uaRelay` (a UA's verify gas depends on its kind: secp256k1 ≈ 0.05 M cap, P-256 0.4 M, a Solidity PQ verify 1.4–5.95 M; a token without a price is refused for a UA payer); for the address `relay` only when its token has a price (owner ruling 2026-10-28 item 7 keeps the flat `min_amount` until before mainnet); a sponsored fee (bound elsewhere, `relay_bound_payee`) is not priced. (7) `ua_metatx` jobs, as `metatx` jobs, get no fee check (every state-changing mtx* is relayable with fee 0, owner 2026-10-20): the "never fails at the relayer's cost" check is the simulation of the exact call, whose estimate covers the kind's verify (the registry hands each verifier its cap only when it can: a starved verify reverts `UAVerifyGas`, never a verdict); a native-id UA with code gets the ERC-1271 floor as on the address path, a derived UA none. (8) The lane's subject is an id (`MetaRef.from: bytes32` + `ua`): the `consumed` check reads `uaNonce(from, batch)` (the one nonce map), the in-flight key is the token's `uaDigest` / `uaTransferDigest`, the classification reads `UAMetaTransactionExecuted`. (9) Indexer: `UAPaymentSettled` and `UAMetaTransactionExecuted` are sent as `PaymentSettled` and `MetaTransactionExecuted` rows with ids (a native id as its address, a derived UA as bytes32 hex), as NEAR and Algorand send their holders, so the client's ingest gains no event name; `PaymentMeta` and a UA payer's `RelayFeePaid` (`payer` = the UA id) join them by `(from, entry_ref)` (and amount and payee), unchanged. (10) Recorded ceilings: the quote is the first send's; a stuck transaction's replacement (`track`, fee bump up to `max_fee_cap_gwei`) can cost more than it; the e2e uses a secp256k1 UA (no Rust signer for a PQ kind here), the PQ verify gas enters only through the simulation. Not built (UA F5): the gateway route `/v1/ua-metatx`, the record cache, mesh `evm.ua_meta_tx`, `UATransfer` / `UA_POOL` pairing, `uaBatch*` / `uaCancelNonce` / `uaPayReceiverFee` jobs. Tests: `metatx::ua_*` (the clientkeys vectors `vectors/ua/metatx3.json`), `submit::ua_*`, `submit::min_wei_value_is_parsed_or_refused`, `indexer::ua_payments_are_payment_rows_and_join_their_meta_and_relay_fee`, e2e `ua_pay_meta_and_relay_fee_jobs_on_anvil` (QUOTE ≥ the lane's ETH cost for both jobs; `scaas-node/runs/2026-10-30-ua-jobs-*.txt`). Cost if wrong: a UA payer's relay fee priced by an operator floor that is too low loses the lane the difference (the operator sets `min_wei_value`); without the price no UA relay fee is served on that token.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review C1, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): the EVM indexer's rows for a derived UA. The client's ingest (the reference ERP connector's `chain_event_ingest`) takes only `0x` + 40 hex for `contract`, `from`, `to`, `fee_recipient` and `relayer` on an EVM chain and refuses the whole range otherwise; a bytes32 id in one row (any derived UA's `UAPaymentSettled` or `UAMetaTransactionExecuted`, e.g. a permissionless `payWithFeeToUA`) would stop the chain's indexer for good. Now a derived id's `from` / `to` is `UA_POOL` (`MetaTxLib.UA_POOL`, the holder ERC-20 observers see for every UA move) and the bytes32 id travels in `from_ua` / `to_ua` (`relay_payee_ua` for a derived bound payee); a native id stays its address. Joins compare the ids (`*_ua` when present), never `UA_POOL`. Supersedes item (9) of the Change above ("bytes32 hex as NEAR / Algorand"). The unit tests and the e2e's fake client run every row through the client's 40-hex rule. Client follow-up (TODO.md): the connector reads `from_ua` / `to_ua`. Checked (report only): the client has no `near` or `algorand` family (`lib/addresses.py` `canonical` raises "unknown network family"), so it refuses every row of those chains today, UA or not; their adapters send a UA holder as `0x` + 64 hex, which the client will have to accept when it adds the families. Cost if wrong: a derived UA's payments show `UA_POOL` in the client until it reads the id keys.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review I1, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): a priced relay-fee job's fee ceiling. The quote is the gas limit × the job's fee ceiling = `FEE_HEADROOM` (2, `guard::FEE_HEADROOM`) × the max fee per gas of its first send (+ the L1 fee, I3), stored per job (`Sent.ceiling`); `track` clamps every replacement of a live priced job at `min(max_fee_cap_gwei, ceiling)`, so at the ceiling it waits ("stuck at the fee cap") and expires; the gap-fill that then takes the nonce uses the operator's cap (21,000 gas, it runs no job). After a restart the first send's ceiling is not journaled, so a tracked priced job's ceiling is its tracked transaction's max fee and it is re-checked (fee × price ≥ gas × that fee) before it can be re-signed; not covered, an unknown fee, or an OP-stack chain ⇒ the nonce is only gap-filled. Not chosen: quoting at `max_fee_cap_gwei` (orders of magnitude too dear) or H = 1 (no replacement passes a mempool's +10 % rule). The generic lane runner signs once and never replaces; its build-time fees are frozen for `sign` (a runner that replaces must clamp at `fee_ceiling`). Tests: `submit::priced_relay_fee_replacements_stay_under_the_job_ceiling`, `submit::a_tracked_priced_relay_job_is_rechecked_after_a_restart`, the e2e's stuck uaRelay (5 sends, the last exactly at the ceiling). Cost if wrong: a job that cannot land under 2 × its first fee expires and the payer re-signs.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review I2, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): a per-subject in-flight hold. A balance drain fails a relayed payment after the inner call and the whole verify (up to ~6 M gas for a Solidity PQ kind), at the lane's cost; through our own node it was free (a fee-0 `ua_metatx` drain on another lane). Now the chain's shared in-flight set also counts, per `subject_key(token, id)`, the relay-fee jobs and the other jobs of a subject: a relay-fee job (`relay`: its address, padded; `uaRelay`: its id) is signed only when no job of that subject on that token is in flight, and no other job of the subject (a `ua_metatx` or `metatx` of it, or another relay-fee job) is signed while one is; a held job is requeued `SUBJECT_HELD` (retried). The hold travels with the digest guard (released when the job leaves the lane), is rebuilt for tracked jobs at a restart, and the generic lane runner takes it too (Hedera). Residual (recorded, priced by the kind's verify until NODE-LANE-15's grief score is built): another relayer's send, a direct transaction of the payer, a plain ERC-20 `transfer`, a DEX leg or `mtxWrap` lowering the balance. Test: `submit::a_relay_fee_job_holds_its_payer`.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review I3, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): the L1 data fee in the quote. On a chain whose config marks it OP-stack (`params.l1_fee = "op-stack"`; any other value a startup error; Base, Celo) the quote of a priced relay-fee job adds `FEE_HEADROOM` × `GasPriceOracle.getL1Fee(raw)` (predeploy `0x420000000000000000000000000000000000000F`) of the signed transaction the lane is about to send (signed, not sent: a refusal consumes no nonce); an oracle that reverts refuses the job (terminal), a transport error retries it. The generic lane runner refuses a priced job on an OP-stack chain (it does not sign before its check). Other rollup fee models (Arbitrum's L1 component in `gasUsed`, which `eth_estimateGas` covers) need no flag. Test: `submit::op_stack_l1_fee_is_in_the_quote`.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review minors, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): (1) `min_wei_value` also takes `"<wei>/<10^k>"` (wei per 10^k base units, the denominator a power of ten) so an 18-decimal token below 1 wei per unit is priced exactly; covered iff `fee × wei >= quote × 10^k` in 256 bits; 0 refuses every priced job; docs say to round a price down. (2) `min_wei_value` without `router`, and one token under two spellings (case), are startup errors. (3) "Below the quote" is a retry (`queued`), not a kill; a missing price for a UA payer stays terminal. (4) The e2e's QUOTE check can fail: a stuck priced uaRelay is replaced while blocks are paused and every send's max fee must stay ≤ 2 × the first (unclamped, the fourth 25 % bump passes it); the unpriced `uaPayMeta` QUOTE line is gone. (5) A native-id UA job's classification reads both `UAMetaTransactionExecuted` and `MetaTransactionExecuted` (one nonce map; `chain::executed_events`). (6) The generic runner's frozen build-time fees are commented (I1). (7) The gate's fixed step logs are copied per feature to `scaas-node/runs/2026-10-30-ua-jobs-fix1-gate-*.txt` with the commit in their first line.

Change (2026-10-30, **owner ruling D4** — SCaaS never calls into a designator where it picks the callee; status: current, decided (owner); commit: `no7702` `955f5337`): (1) `MtxRelayFee._shape`: `!SigCheck.isContract(target)` ⇒ `RelayTargetNoCode(target)` (was `target.code.length == 0`). This is also a **bug fix**: a designator pointing at a code-less address passed the old check and the call succeeded empty, so the payer paid for nothing (the very case `RelayTargetNoCode` exists for); one pointing at code ran the delegate as the executor's callee. (2) `WrappedLib.payOut`, `NATIVE` leg: a designator recipient is refused with `UnwrapRecipientInvalid(recipient)` (`unwrap` and the Zether / PQZ unshield-unwrap `payOutTo`); an ERC-20 leg may still pay a designator (a plain ERC-20 runs no recipient code; an outside token with ERC-777 / ERC-1363 hooks may, on a recipient the unwrapper chose). Left as they are (owner-chosen or solver-chosen, conservation-checked): `MandateWallet` / `SmartKeyAccount` `execute` targets and DEX `_interact` targets. Why: "an EOA must not run code" — a native-coin send runs the delegate with all forwarded gas. Cost if wrong: a 7702 user cannot receive native coin through `unwrap` while delegated (it unwraps to another address or clears its delegation). The router's bytecode changed (+74 B), so its CREATE2 address moves: redeploy (all chains are test-only). Tests: `test_relay_targetDesignatorRefused`, `test_native_unwrapToDesignatorRefused`. Source: the EIP-7702 audit of 2026-10-30 (`research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md`) §4 T1–T4.
